- Head of ML infra: wants a detailed cost model by commit level (monthly GPU equivalent), utilization sensitivity, and per-token unit economics.

Commercial: evaluating 6 / 12 month reserved commit (24 -> 72 GPU-eq tiers). They asked Redwood to show ARR impact with utilization bands: 40%, 60%, 80%, 95%. Want price breakpoints at those utilization levels and SLA credit terms for p99 > target.

Current negotiation points:

- Sovereign counter: requires capped unit cost per 1k tokens at 60% util, additional uplift if p99 SLA missed.
- Legal: needs SOC2 addendum + data residency clause before procurement.

Internal notes: AE to push model-mix quantization options (8-bit + INT8) and batching strategies from Optimize team to reduce committed GPU count. SE to run batch sizing study (Drive sheet link).

use_case_summary: Primary: real-time underwriting assistant (chat) + high-volume embedding index for similarity search + reranking for fraud signals. Needs predictable latency for underwriting (p99 SLA), cost-sensitive embedding workloads (batch), and deterministic routing for regulated flows.
cost_model_assumptions: Proposal assumptions used in model.xlsx: commit tiers expressed as GPU-month equivalents (24, 36, 48, 72). Baseline unit economics: assume A100-equivalent pricing; base price per committed GPU-month = quoted_rate (confidential). Utilization scenarios: 40% / 60% / 80% / 95%. Token economics derived from measured tokens/sec at production batch sizes: chat workload ~ 1.4k tokens/sec per A100-eq at avg gen length 45 tokens; embeddings throughput measured as 1.8M vectors/day per 24-GPU pod. Unit price sensitivity: at 60% util target, effective cost per 1k tokens = modeled_rate_60 (drive sheet); at 80% util = modeled_rate_80; requested Redwood to provide break-even points where Dedicated beats hosted API including egress and caching. Also asked for explicit SLA credit language: sliding credit tied to p99 breaches and sustained underprovisioning during peak windows.
